text:
**For a full recharge in one day, plan on roughly 250-350 W of panels. A 200 W panel will do it in about a day and a half.**

**The formula**

Panel watts ≈ 1,000 Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75). The 0.7-0.75 covers heat, panel angle, and charge-controller losses ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)).

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts for a 1-day recharge from empty |
|---|---|
| 3 (shoulder season) | ~450 W |
| 4 (typical) | ~340 W |
| 5 (good summer day) | ~270 W |
| 6 (Southwest summer) | ~230 W |

Source: [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/). Another guide estimates about 300 W in summer and 700 W or more in a northern winter ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

**Practical rules of thumb**
- **200 W panel:** It yields about 630 Wh on an average day (4.5 sun hours × 70%), so it refills 1,000 Wh in roughly 1.5 days ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station)).
- **Quick check:** Divide the battery's Wh by 5 to get the panel wattage that recharges it in about 1.5 days of decent sun ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **Winter or cloudy weather:** Output can fall to 10-25% of normal under solid cloud, so size for your worst month.
- **Using the station while it charges:** Any load you run reduces the net charge.

**Check before buying**
1. **Max solar input watts:** Your station caps what it accepts. Many 1,000 Wh units take 200-400 W or more, and panels beyond the cap add nothing.
2. **Input voltage window:** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside your station's range. Going over can damage it, and panels wired in series add voltage.
3. **Connector type:** Check for MC4, XT60, or DC barrel, and whether an adapter is included.

**One option if you want a fast, one-day recharge**
The [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W foldable panel](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel) is listed at $299, or $269.10 with code ALLPOWERS26. The code was reported as tested on 2026-10-21 and expires 2026-12-30. It has a Voc of 45.3 V, so it only suits stations that accept that voltage. It's also heavy at 18.5 kg. The listing says it's too high-voltage for some small stations, such as the Tenergy T320 and BLUETTI Elite 30 V2. That link is an affiliate link, and the store's checkout has the final word on price. If your station's solar input is capped below 400 W, a smaller panel is the better buy.
